headline: Clear the lowest set bit once per iteration
statement: Given a positive integer n, return the number of 1 bits in its binary representation, also called its Hamming weight.
intuition: Clear one set bit at a time. The operation n & (n - 1) removes the rightmost 1 from a positive binary number while leaving the other 1s intact. Count how many times this can be done before the number becomes zero.
approach: While n is nonzero, replace it with n & (n-1) and increment count.
Return count when every set bit has been removed.
correctness: For any positive n, the transformation n&(n-1) clears exactly its least significant set bit and no other set bit. After t iterations, count=t and exactly t original set bits have been removed. The loop ends when none remain, so count is the original Hamming weight.
bruteForce: Inspect each bit position with a mask or repeatedly shift and test n&1. That takes O(bit width) even for sparse values.

complexity.explanation: At most 31 iterations are needed under the stated input bound.

pitfalls: Use bitwise AND, not logical and.
Do not count the bit length: 128 has eight binary positions but one set bit.
Keep a count before mutating n, whose final value is zero.
